clue.text: Shock vote for right — nothing smart

parts.note: to vote for someone is to elect them
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
smart in the sense of clever or shrewd is cute

explanation.surface: A ballot for the right wing that nobody would call clever comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like an adjective describing the vote, but it is a verb defining the answer; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrocute is to kill or injure with a powerful electric jolt.

clue.text: Tories upset after labour leader wastes time

indicators.note: after places the shuffled Tories behind the letter taken from labour
the leader of the word labour is its opening letter
upset tells us the letters of Tories are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Conservatives are put out when the Labour leader dawdles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labour' is not the party here; only its leading letter is used, and 'upset' is the anagram signal for the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loiters hangs about idly, frittering away the hours.

clue.text: Agreeable politician on left in frantic action

indicators.note: in puts the politician and left inside the rearranged letters
frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters of action are rearranged

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A cooperative MP of the Left caught up in some frenzied activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' rearranges ACTION into CO-IANT, and 'in' places MP plus L in the gap, giving CO-MPL-IANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A compliant person goes along with requests, so is accommodating and willing.

clue.text: Predicts socialists to hold American capital

indicators.note: to hold means the socialists wrap around the next piece

parts.note: Reds is a common name for socialists or communists

indicators.note: the capital of the word American is its first letter

explanation.surface: Forecasts that left-wingers will keep hold of American money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but here means the capital (first) letter of 'American', A, which REDS holds.
explanation.definitionFit: One reads the future, tea leaves or the stars when foretelling what will happen.

clue.text: Arthur's seat?

parts.note: Arthur's Seat is a hill in Edinburgh, but read literally it asks where King Arthur held court

explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is a well-known hill overlooking Edinburgh; the question mark invites the other reading, the legendary king's home castle.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the castle and court of King Arthur was his seat of power.

clue.text: Storm wracked by trouble

parts.note: wracked, torn apart or ruined, gives torn
ado is fuss or bother, so trouble

explanation.surface: A tempest tearing everything apart and causing havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wracked' looks like an anagram signal, but it supplies TORN; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling wind, a type of tempest.

clue.text: Reckless fling?

explanation.surface: A hasty, ill-judged affair.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means rash or headlong; as a verb it means hurl down or throw violently.

clue.text: Seat's sound for posture

indicators.note: sound here means the word for a seat is said out loud

parts.note: a country seat is a manor house

explanation.surface: How one sits is the right stance for good bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'seat' is a stately country home, a MANOR, which said out loud matches the answer; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner is bearing or deportment, the way one carries oneself.

clue.text: State one's in shows common sense

indicators.note: in tells us the next piece sits inside the state

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom or state
one's read as one is: I, the Roman numeral for one, followed by S

explanation.surface: A nation's being represented shows practical wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', the Roman numeral for one followed by the abbreviation for is; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a practical, down-to-earth outlook that faces facts sensibly.

clue.text: 'Respect' dead in a pickle

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for dead within the other pieces

parts.note: a pickle is a predicament or mess, as is a mire

explanation.surface: An old song title found in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: D (dead) goes inside A MIRE, between A and MIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to hold them in high regard, to esteem them.

clue.text: Unusual lapse in Tory character

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of lapse in Tory appear in an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: A rare slip-up by a Conservative reveals his true nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' signals the anagram of all eleven letters of 'lapse in Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: Personality is the set of traits that make up a person's nature.

clue.text: Cool criminal getting bird. E's inside!

parts.note: con, short for convict, is a criminal

indicators.note: inside means the letter is set within the word for a girl

parts.note: bird is British slang for a girl or gal
the clue's E is the letter E

explanation.surface: A cool crook gets a girlfriend, but someone named E is the insider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a young woman; 'E's inside!' reads like a news flash but tells you where the letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to set or thicken as a liquid cools and solidifies.

clue.text: Liberal in violent scrap

indicators.note: in places the Liberal abbreviation inside the word for violent

parts.note: savage means fierce or violent
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: A Liberal caught up in a vicious fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight to go with 'violent', but it is the noun for waste material.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is material rescued from a wreck or waste for reuse.

clue.text: Place amorous romance is started initially?

definitions.text: Place amorous romance is started initially?

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the preceding five words

explanation.surface: Where is the spot that love affairs begin?
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'Place amorous romance is started' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes the city famed for love.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital is widely called the city of love, where romance blooms.

clue.text: Three under for handicap

explanation.surface: A golfer three shots below par despite a handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, scoring three under par on a hole is an albatross; the bird hung round the Ancient Mariner's neck made it a byword for a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call a hole played three strokes below par this; figuratively it is a heavy burden or encumbrance.

clue.text: He provides for drinking spree taking skill

indicators.note: taking means the drinking spree takes the skill inside it

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A supplier of booze for a binge that takes some expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He provides for drinking' sounds like a host's generosity, but it defines a job; 'taking' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The person behind a bar serves the customers their beer and spirits.

clue.text: Bully backing rubbish teacher

indicators.note: backing tells us the word for rubbish runs back to front

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
a mentor is a guide or teacher

explanation.surface: A bully supporting a useless schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it reverses ROT to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor persecutes and harasses others, as a bully does.

clue.text: Far out in east, admitting habit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Far out in east, admitting habit (7)' for ROUTINE: the definition is habit, but no reading of 'Far out in east, admitting' builds ROUTINE (OUT, IN, E leave an R unexplained), and a search of the exact text found no source.
annotationWithheld.clue: Far out in east, admitting habit

clue.text: More vacuous setter's flipping awful tripe

indicators.note: flipping means the setter's word for himself is turned over

parts.note: a setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of tripe are in a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's damned dreadful rubbish is even emptier-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild oath but reverses ME to EM; 'awful' rearranges TRIPE into PTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier is the comparative of empty, meaning lacking more in content or sense.

clue.text: Major ganglia — part of the brain, perhaps

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the words Major ganglia

explanation.surface: Big clusters of nerve cells forming a section of the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'majOR GANglia'; 'perhaps' signals that the brain is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is one example of a body part with a specific function, like the heart or liver.

clue.text: Ham finished with a case of claret

parts.note: over means finished or ended

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: An overdone actor polished off with a crate of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'case of claret' gives CT, the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way.

clue.text: Crew on middle of test river

parts.note: a gang is a crew or team

indicators.note: middle of means take the central letters of the word test

explanation.surface: A team is on the middle of a test, perhaps a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test' suggests an exam or a cricket Test match, but only its central pair of letters is used; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred river of northern India.

clue.text: Call topless tart

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a strumpet is a prostitute, which tart can mean

explanation.surface: Summon a woman with nothing on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' is not pastry but a prostitute, STRUMPET; dropping its first letter S gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet is to proclaim or announce loudly, as a bugle call does.

clue.text: Strip taking this off?

parts.note: strip is both a narrow piece of leather and what a stripper does as the last garment comes off

explanation.walkthrough: A strip can be a narrow band of leather; the question mark hints at a striptease, where the skimpy undergarment is the last thing removed.
explanation.definitionFit: This skimpy undergarment is a final item removed in a striptease, and the word also means a leather strap.

clue.text: English bird — utterly, endlessly timeless

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: all, as in all gone, means utterly or completely

explanation.surface: A thoroughly English seabird that seems to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' gives ALL (as in 'all alone'), and 'endlessly' trims it to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal has no beginning or end, existing outside time.

clue.text: Automatic drive?

parts.note: reads like a car gearbox, but drive is an instinctive urge that works without being willed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Automatic drive' suggests a car's transmission; the question mark points to an involuntary urge, the sexual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is the sex drive, an urge that arises instinctively rather than by choice.

clue.text: Darling of French has absolute support

parts.note: de is the French word for of
A is an abbreviation for absolute, as in the absolute temperature scale
a rest is a prop or support

explanation.surface: A French sweetheart has total backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. A for 'absolute' is a dictionary abbreviation from science, used for absolute temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearest is a term of endearment for a loved one, like sweetheart.

clue.text: Keep cool about great fire spreading

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters of great fire are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Stay calm about a huge blaze that is spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) comes first, then 'spreading' rearranges GREATFIRE into FRIGERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrigerate food is to chill it to preserve it.
